descripcion:
Everyone laughed at his "cheese grater" coins. Then the king's scale stopped moving. 🪙⚖️

Look at the edge of an old-style coin and you'll see tiny ridges. They weren't there for decoration. When coins were made of real gold and silver, people could shave metal off the smooth edges and still spend them at full value. It was called clipping. Ridged edges made a shaved coin easy to spot.

Would you have spotted the clue before the king did? 👇

This story and its characters are fictional. Coin clipping and ridged edges are real history: England's new machine-made coins with milled edges replaced old hammered silver in the Great Recoinage of 1696, with Isaac Newton at the Royal Mint.
